name: laptop_dmic
_notes: Stand-in array: the ThinkPad T14s' 2-channel DMIC pair on the lid (owner B's dev profile).
Same shape as config/array.json so ingest/DOA/fusion are geometry-agnostic; swapping in the
hat is `--profile hat` and nothing else. This is NOT the wearable and must never be claimed as it.
Channels are the device channel order from pw-record (audio.position FL,FR): 0 = left, 1 = right.
x is the hat frame axis (0deg bearing = +y = nose); with the lid as the array, +x = wearer right.
spacing_m starts null: the real value is measured, never assumed. The measured value is
filled in automatically by `server/main.py --fit-spacing write`, which borrows the camera
bearing while someone talks (server/calib_fit.py) and writes back into this file.
Until then DOA still measures the real sign, and accuracy_deg is deliberately huge.
highpass_hz/lowpass_hz are required on this laptop and are set to the DOA band itself:
the DMIC pair arrives with a large DC offset (ch1 +5160 LSB), a spectral rise below 250 Hz
and a second rise above 6 kHz (+68 dB at Nyquist). Measured with a clap played from the
speakers: 5.6 dB above the room unfiltered, 26 dB once the junk is band-passed away, and
0 onsets detected unfiltered vs every clap detected filtered. See server/ingest.py BandPass.
device: the PipeWire node name of the DMIC array; null = whatever the default source is.
